note: Corps of Engineers campground on the Grand River arm of Truman Lake south of Clinton, in two wooded loops on a point: Loop A (56 sites with electric and water) and Loop B (27 electric-only sites) 400 m south. A few Loop A pads look down an open slope to a cove about 70 m off. Boat ramp, playground and laundry. --Claude
summary: rec.gov read (USACE's own pages refused, unread): season Mar 1-Nov 30, $30-35 peak and $14 off-peak (the stored $14 low is the shoulder-season rate), 83 electric sites 45-91 ft, water at the 56 Loop A sites, showers/flush/laundry/dump. Weekend 2-night and holiday 3-night minimums written. Lakeview stands. PIN MOVE proposed onto Loop A. Electric amperage conflict flagged, not written.

WATERFRONT (stored lakeview, evidence was a commit reference only; no change): counted on the 0.37 m/px leaf-off frame with site coordinates plotted. Nearest sites to water are A16, A17, A18, A19 on the east edge of Loop A, 65-75 m from the head of a cove, across an open grass slope with scattered trees - a clear view, but outside 50 m, and the cove head is shallow and draws down. A20/A21 are about 75 m from the next cove through trees. Every other Loop A site and all of Loop B (B19/B40 about 90-100 m from the shore, wooded) are farther. On an open apron within 50 m: none. Lakeview is right. rec.gov's facility-level 'Waterfront Sites' amenity is not per-site evidence; no site carries a Proximity to Water value.
